item.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, but Zelensky says it's news to him
item.description:
President Donald Trump claimed Sunday that Ukraine and Russia have agreed to an “energy ceasefire” as part of the ongoing conflict. There was no immediate confirmation from Moscow, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reportedly said this “was news for me.”

Trump made a similar announcement a month ago, only for the two sides to continue their aerial attacks on each other’s energy facilities.

“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday morning. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” He did not elaborate further on what the ceasefire might include.

Zelenskyy told Axios that he knew nothing about a ceasefire deal.

“But if Russians agree to an energy ceasefire Ukraine will agree,” Zelenskyy said, according to Axios. “If President Trump negotiated it with [Russian President Vladimir] Putin — please tell us when the ceasefire begins — we are ready and we will accept it.”

NBC News has reached out to Zelenskyy’s office for further comment.

It follows a dramatic few days in which Trump agreed to a diesel deal with the Kremlin, demanded Kyiv halt attacks on Russian oil refineries and called for Zelenskyy to be replaced. The shift left Kyiv and its European allies reeling.

The U.S. agreed Friday to lift sanctions on Russian fuel in a deal that Trump said would see Russia “immediately” release 300,000 tons of diesel “to the American and global marketplace,” followed by 500,000 tons in November and another million after that.

After strong criticism from Zelenskyy, Trump said Saturday: “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals.”

Trump has sought to blame the Ukraine conflict, rather than his own assault on Iran, for a global fuel shortage that has driven diesel prices to record highs since the U.S. launched the Middle East war in February.

Zelenskyy reiterated Sunday that he was ready to halt strikes on Russian refineries if the Kremlin halts its own attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

“We are ready for energy ceasefire, not to attack energy — both sides,” he said in an interview on ABC News’ “This Week.” He added that if Russia wants an energy ceasefire, “we are open for this.”

“Don’t attack us,” he said. “Don’t kill our children. We will stop attack your diesel.”

He also told ABC News he would hold elections if Russia agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.

Zelenskyy said “it’s up to Ukrainians” to choose their leader and noted that Putin would also like to ​change who is ​leading Ukraine.

He ⁠said it is easy for Ukraine to be blamed for higher fuel ​prices “when everybody in the world understands [that] ​because ⁠of the war in [the] Middle East, the prices are rising.”

Zelenskyy was also asked on ABC News why Trump and Elon Musk blamed him for the war’s continuation.

“Because these people can’t find a key how to stop Putin, because it’s more difficult to stop Putin than to pressure others, because it’s more simple to speak about the prices and connect it with Ukraine,” he responded, pointing to how the war in Iran was leading to higher fuel prices.

This article was originally published on NBCNews.com

This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/trump-russia-ukraine-agree-energy-ceasefire-zelenskyy-diesel-rcna602766

item.title: 泽连斯基把选举与俄方60天停火挂钩
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

乌克兰总统泽连斯基10月11日表示，如果俄罗斯总统普京同意全面停火60天，乌克兰就可以组织选举。此前，美国总统川普公开表示“乌克兰是时候换新总统了”，并批评泽连斯基错失多次结束战争的机会。泽连斯基接受ABC采访时回应称，乌克兰领导人应由乌克兰人民选择，但当前战争和戒严状态使选举面临安全及法律困难。

泽连斯基说：“请转告普京，给我们两个月、60天的全面停火，我们就会组织选举。”他同时表示，如果俄罗斯停止袭击乌克兰能源设施，乌方也愿意停止攻击俄罗斯炼油厂。此前川普要求乌克兰单方面停止相关袭击，并将美国柴油价格上涨部分归因于乌方行动。

乌克兰在戒严状态下举行全国选举确实面临实际困难，包括前线军人如何投票、数百万海外居民如何参与、被占地区选民安排以及投票站安全等。但“必须先全面停火60天”并不是战时选举的一项国际通行规则，也不是一个无需解释的客观期限。

俄罗斯本身就是一个现成的对照。2024年3月俄乌战争仍在持续时，俄罗斯照常举行总统选举；投票期间俄罗斯境内仍遭到乌克兰袭击，战争并未因为选举而暂停。该次选举的自由和公平程度受到西方政府和独立观察人士严重质疑，但它至少说明，战争持续本身并不等于全国选举在技术上绝对无法举行。

因此，泽连斯基提出的“60天”更适合被理解为他设定的政治和安全条件，而不是已经得到证明的必需期限。为什么是60天，而不是30天、45天或90天，目前也没有看到他给出具体法律或行政依据。

这还带来一个值得注意的问题：乌克兰的选举属于本国宪政程序，如果是否举行选举必须以俄罗斯是否同意60天停火为前提，那么普京事实上也就获得了影响乌克兰选举时间的能力。

泽连斯基这一表态在政治传播上很有效——它把川普提出的“换总统”压力反推给莫斯科：如果俄罗斯愿意停火，乌克兰就选。但从事实层面，更准确的说法仍然是：乌克兰战时举行选举困难很大；“全面停火60天”则是泽连斯基提出的条件，而不是已经被证明不可替代的客观门槛。

关键词: 
选举
栏目: 
时事见解
作者: 
司空墨海

item.title: 川普宣布俄乌达成“能源停火” 立即生效
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

美国总统川普10月11日宣布，俄罗斯与乌克兰已经同意实施“能源停火”，并称协议立即生效。川普在社交媒体发文说，俄乌双方都已同意这一安排，并警告双方“不要破坏它”。

川普没有说明“能源停火”的具体范围，也没有公布协议文本、期限、核查机制或违约处理办法。路透报道，截至川普宣布消息时，基辅和莫斯科尚未分别正式确认协议细节，因此目前仍需观察双方是否真正停止相关袭击。

连斯基当天稍早提出的对等方案。泽连斯基表示，如果俄罗斯停止攻击乌克兰电力及其他能源基础设施，乌克兰也愿意停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，并强调任何缓和措施都必须是双方对等实施，并有实际保障。

此前，川普曾要求乌克兰停止攻击俄罗斯炼油厂，并把美国柴油价格大幅上涨部分归因于乌方行动。美国柴油价格今年以来受到中东战争、全球成品油供应紧张以及俄乌战争影响大幅上涨。川普本周还与俄罗斯总统普京达成柴油供应安排，暂时放松部分针对俄罗斯燃料交易的限制。

如果能源停火得到俄乌双方确认并执行，意味着川普此前要求乌克兰单方面停止袭击俄炼油厂，最终转化为双方同时停止攻击对方能源设施的安排。

不过，这仍然只是局部停火，并非俄乌战争全面停火。双方前线作战、导弹和无人机针对其他军事及基础设施目标的攻击是否继续，目前没有改变的明确信息。

泽连斯基同日还表示，如果俄罗斯同意全面停火60天，乌克兰可以组织总统选举。因此，即使川普宣布的能源停火顺利执行，也并未满足泽连斯基所提出的“60天全面停火”条件。

目前最关键的问题，是双方是否会在未来数日真正停止袭击炼油厂、电站、输电设施等能源目标，以及这项有限停火能否进一步扩大为更广泛的军事停火。

关键词: 
停火
栏目: 
时事见解

卞一之

item.title: Pregnant woman was days away from giving birth when she was killed in Pa. shooting
item.description:
NEED TO KNOW

  • Angelina Stone was among the nine people killed in a mass shooting in Pennsylvania on Friday, Oct. 9
  • A family friend said that Stone was just days from giving birth
  • Investigators believe that the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound in the incident, during which two children also died

A pregnant woman was among the nine people killed in a mass shooting in Pennsylvania. 

Angelina Stone and her loved ones were identified as victims of the shooting that occurred at a home in Erie, Pa. around 5 p.m. local time on Friday, Oct. 9, according to CBS News. 

The news outlet reported that Stone was just four days from giving birth. The victims also included her two children, brothers and a friend. 

Family friend Lisa Simmers told CBS News, “Her two babies were on the spectrum. Innocent children, couldn’t have told on that man if they wanted to, and he still killed them.”

She added, “It’s mind-blowing to me to understand what was happening in that house while we were standing outside. The feeling of helplessness and knowing we couldn’t do anything and she was right there.” 

Simmers told Erie News Now that Stone had a “beautiful” family.

“She was pregnant, about to have her baby in a couple of days. She had a daughter that was almost two, and her son Isiah, who I believe was like four or five, and they were all just beautiful. Beautiful children. And definitely did not deserve what happened to them,” the friend said.

A GoFundMe has been created to raise funds for Stone and her children’s funeral arrangements. The fundraiser identifies Stone’s children as son Isiah, daughter Amari’anna and unborn baby Kyrie.

“We have no finances ready to cover this loss, and we have only two weeks from today to get everything done. The funds from this fundraiser will go toward funeral expenses and the fees related to their final arrangements so they can be sent off correctly. This is more than our family can carry alone right now, and we truly need the community to rally around us,” the description for the fundrasier reads.

PEOPLE reached out to the Erie County Sheriff’s Office on Sunday, Oct. 11, but did not immediately hear back. 

A press release on Saturday, Oct. 10 stated that police arrived on the scene within minutes of receiving the alert. 

The nine deaths occurred before officers arrived, according to the investigation. There were no additional gunshots after police arrived.

“Our hearts remain with the victims, their loved ones, and all those affected by this devastating loss of life,” the City of Erie said in the release.

Want to keep up with the latest crime coverage? Sign up for PEOPLE’s free True Crime newsletter for breaking crime news, ongoing trial coverage and details of intriguing unsolved cases.

Chief of Police Richard Lorah later said in a press conference that police found two deceased females outside the residence within minutes of arriving.

“Video evidence reviewed by investigators shows those two women arriving at the residence, hearing distress, seeking assistance from neighbors and pounding on the door. The audio video also appears to capture muffled gunfire from inside the residence before the suspect emerged and fatally shot both women,” he said. 

Based on evidence so far, investigators believe that the suspect died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. 

The nine dead individuals included eight family members and one family friend.

Lorah also stated that one of the victims was “eight months pregnant.”

Victims included a 51-year-old female and a 37-year-old female found outside the residence; a 5-year-old boy and a 1-year-old girl were found on the first floor, and a 24-year-old female, a 44-year-old female, a 19-year-old male and a 21-year-old male on the second floor and stairwell.

The suspected shooter, a 45-year-old, was found dead on the second floor with a firearm.

“Some scenes some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes,” Lorah said.

Read the original article on People

This article originally appeared on People at https://people.com/pregnant-woman-was-days-from-giving-birth-when-she-was-killed-penn-mass-shooting-12169256

item.title: U.K. PM Burnham says Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
item.description:
By Andrew MacAskill

LONDON, Oct 11 (Reuters) - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit vote, as he warned voters in France and ‌Germany about Moscow-backed efforts to influence their politics.

Burnham, who took over as Britain's ‌leader in July and said last month that Britain could consider rejoining the European Union in the future, ​is the first British prime minister to say openly there was evidence of Russian interference in the referendum a decade ago.

"I asked the question coming to Downing Street, was there interference in the 2016 referendum from Russia? And I've had the clear answer that yes, there was," Burnham ‌said in an interview with ⁠The Rest Is Politics podcast released on Sunday.

Burnham did not spell out how he believed that Russia interfered in the referendum and gave no ⁠details on what evidence this statement was based.

The Russian embassy in London did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Russia has previously denied meddling in the Brexit vote, casting Britain as ​gripped by ​anti-Russian hysteria.

Burnham's comments mark a departure from those ​of former Prime Minister Boris Johnson, ‌who campaigned to leave the EU, and said in 2020 there was no evidence of Russian interference in the referendum.

Britons voted 52%-48% to leave the EU in 2016, plunging the country into its biggest political crisis since World War Two.

Burnham said voters in European democracies needed to be better informed about efforts to disrupt their politics.

"I mean, these things are ‌important now to put clearly on the record, and ​I believe, help voters in Germany and France understand ​that some of this politics is ​instigated via our enemies, namely Russia," he said.

Britain's government failed to establish ‌whether Russia meddled in the 2016 referendum ​on membership of the ​EU, according to a report by parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee in 2020.

The report also found that Russia had sought to influence Scotland's 2014 independence referendum, in which ​voters rejected independence.

Burnham last month ‌said he could campaign to take Britain back into the EU at the ​next general election, reopening the country’s divisive debate on its relationship with ​the continent.

(Reporting by Andrew MacAskillEditing by Alexandra Hudson)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://uk.news.yahoo.com/uk-pm-burnham-says-russia-165702257.html

item.title: 贝森特：川普政府有权落实俄柴油协议
item.description:
来源:

美国财政部长贝森特11日表示，川普政府将利用现有法律授权，落实与俄罗斯达成的柴油供应协议，并称国会中任何认为现行对俄制裁法禁止政府这样做的人“都是错误的”。

川普此前宣布，俄罗斯将立即向美国及全球市场供应逾30万吨柴油，11月再供应50万吨，随后增加100万吨。财政部已通过一般许可证，临时放宽相关交易限制至明年4月。

乌克兰总统泽连斯基和多名民主党议员批评协议削弱对俄施压，并可能增加莫斯科能源收入。贝森特则强调，协议有助降低美国柴油价格。现行对俄制裁法律确实保留总统豁免权以及财政部签发一般许可证的权限，因此争议重点更在政策效果及行政部门是否依程序行使授权，而非政府是否完全没有法律依据。

item.title: 6 senators call for White House to 'immediately reverse course' on Russian diesel plan
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A bipartisan group of six senators on Sunday called for President Donald Trump's administration to “immediately reverse course” on a plan to purchase diesel from Russia as part of an effort to lower high fuel prices.

Trump shocked lawmakers when he announced on social media Friday that he struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call. He said Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the American and global market, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.” Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.

Four Republican senators and two Democratic senators signed onto the statement released Sunday in protesting the deal. They said the administration failed to consult with Congress or submit any explanation to justify its decision as required by statute.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians. The Administration must immediately reverse course,” they wrote.

The Republican senators who signed onto the statement are Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Curtis of Utah. The Democratic senators are Sens. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire and Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut.

Tillis, in an interview that aired Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press,” said there's a legitimate case for saying the president is not following the law if the administration goes through with its diesel purchase plan.

“We were very clear that Russia is the aggressor. Russia is the one who can end this war by backing out of territory that they occupied,” Tillis said.

Trump's announcement came just a few weeks after Congress passed legislation that directed Trump to impose substantial tariffs on the top importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

The congressional effort was aimed at cutting the flow of money Russia receives from oil and gas sales to finance its war against Ukraine.

The lawmakers also noted that Congress explicitly banned Russia energy imports in 2022 to prevent the United States from financing the war.

“Congress was clear: the U.S. should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our NATO Allies,” the six lawmakers wrote in their statement. “President Trump’s decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the U.S. runs directly counter to that law.”

Sen. John Barrasso, R-Wyo., said Trump is focused on reducing the cost of energy when asked whether the president's action would be in violation of U.S. law.

“The president is balancing and has to make tough decisions,” Barrasso said on CBS's “Face the Nation.”

He also encouraged Trump to enforce the sanctions law that Congress passed last month.

“This is just another point of leverage for the president to use against Putin in an effort to get a long-term solution in that part of the world,” Barrasso said.

Energy experts say the Russia deal is unlikely to make a dent in high prices at the pump.

Richard Nephew, a senior research scholar at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy, noted that the total amount of diesel appears to be less than what the U.S. uses in a day.

Nephew argued that Iran and Russia might benefit more than the U.S.

“The Iranians are probably very excited because it shows that there’s a lot of pressure still on the U.S. And the Russians are excited because it puts a big hole in the sanctions regime,” he said.

Trump has recently sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than the U.S.-led war in Iran, which has elevated world energy prices.

—-

Associated Press writer Mae Anderson in New York contributed to this report.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/six-senators-call-trump-administration-173315508.html

item.title: DHS secretary Mullin defends planned livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
item.description:
Washington — Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Sunday defended the Pentagon's plan to livestream the execution of an ex-Army major who was convicted of the 2009 killing of 13 people at Fort Hood, while saying that he doesn't see an "elevated risk" to U.S. security amid criticism. 

"I think people need to understand, if you attack America, we will come after you and we will make sure that the punishment fits the crime," Mullin said on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said last week that the Pentagon planned to publicly livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, who is set to die by firing squad on Dec. 3 in what will be the first military execution since 1961. The announcement sparked intense criticism, including from some Republicans, like Sen. Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, who urged the Pentagon to reverse the "gruesome decision," saying there is "no need to livestream any execution, including this one."

"I would expect this from terrorists and dictators, but not here in America," Murkowski wrote in a post on X. "It would give this individual, who deserves no further notoriety, the martyrdom he seeks."

While Mullin defended the Pentagon's move, he said, "No one has to watch it if they don't choose to."

"I follow President Trump. He's the commander in chief of the country, and he does a phenomenal job," Mullin said. "He leads this country with a very, very, very direct, forward, straight hand, and he's restoring America values."

Mullin added that he has "no sympathy" for Hasan, adding, "I give absolutely zero thought to the way that this man dies."

"My job as secretary of homeland security is to protect the homeland, and that's what we do," Mullin said. 

The comments come as Vice President JD Vance on Friday cast some doubt on whether the Pentagon will go ahead with the plan, saying he would not tune in if the livestream happens. The vice president said Hasan committed "the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11" when he killed 13 people and wounded more than 30 others in the attack on the Fort Hood Army base in Texas in 2009.

"So whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people," Vance said. "Now that said, I mean, look, if it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it."

Mr. Trump told reporters on Saturday that there are two schools of thought on whether to livestream the execution, saying, "I'll make a decision, ultimately."

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/markwayne-mullin-nidal-hasan-public-execution-pentagon/

item.title: Brian Fitzpatrick won by 13 points in 2024. Now, Democrats smell blood in the water.
item.description:
YARDLEY, Pennsylvania — Republican Brian Fitzpatrick sailed to reelection in Pennsylvania’s first congressional district two years ago. But now, with just over three weeks to go until Election Day and public opinion continuing to sour on Donald Trump’s presidency, Democrats smell blood in the water.

Their optimism that Fitzpatrick’s Democratic opponent, Bucks County commissioner Bob Harvie, can defeat the five-term incumbent was on display on Saturday afternoon, as Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries and Pennsylvania’s Democratic Gov. Josh Shapiro hit the campaign trail in the leafy Philadelphia suburbs to drum up support for Harvie.

“A lot of people look at this race and think, ‘Well, this is not really one that Democrats can win,’” Harvie told POLITICO after a rally in a middle school gym in Lower Bucks County, where supporters waved red signs emblazoned with the slogan: “Fire Fitz.”

“Clearly they are wrong because Leader Jeffries thinks we can win it,” Harvie said. “Governor Shapiro thinks we can win it.”

Jeffries’ decision to campaign alongside Harvie in the final stretch underscores Democrats’ growing bullishness heading into next month’s midterms, when they aim to retake control of the House of Representatives and usher in a 2018-style “blue wave.”

But it also illustrates the potentially risky bets party operatives are willing to place in the final stretch of campaigning, as they deploy relatively thin resources to try and expand their electoral map, including in districts that were previously seen as out of reach.

In recent days, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee has committed to spending $900,000 in its bid to unseat Fitzpatrick. House Majority PAC, the House Democrats' main super PAC, has spent more than $6 million to reserve television advertisements in the race, according to the latest AdImpact data.

“We are running through the finish line,” Jeffries told reporters after Saturday’s rally. “We take nothing for granted, but we are on the verge of taking back control of the House of Representatives.”

Democratic operatives in the state insist Harvie is within striking distance of flipping the district, which spans all of Bucks County and a sliver of Montgomery County in the affluent Philadelphia suburbs.

A new internal poll conducted last week by Democratic pollsters Global Strategy Group found Harvie and Fitzpatrick tied, 46%-46%, among likely voters, with 8% still undecided.

In a memo first seen by POLITICO, the pollsters argued undecided swing voters would be more likely to break for Harvie in the final weeks of campaigning, noting 60% of undecideds said they would prefer Democrats take back control of Congress.

Still, Democratic leaders acknowledge that even in an increasingly favorable political environment for their party, the odds may be stacked against Harvie.

Separate internal polling commissioned by the Fitzpatrick campaign and the National Republican Congressional Committee last month showed Fitzpatrick leading Harvie by a 9-point margin. And despite the last-minute cash injection from national Democrats in the district, Fitzpatrick has long enjoyed a sizable fundraising advantage. The latest quarterly Federal Election Commission filings showed Fitzpatrick’s campaign spent nearly $5 million on the race in the first six months of the year alone.

"Bob [Harvie] is running a great campaign. Brian [Fitzpatrick] is running a tough campaign,” Shapiro told POLITICO at a separate stop with Democratic Party volunteers earlier on Saturday. “This is one that is going to be really close."

Fitzpatrick, a former FBI special agent who was first elected to Congress in 2016, is widely seen as a strong candidate in Bucks County, a perennial electoral battleground at the presidential level that Shapiro has repeatedly described as the “swingiest county in the swingiest state in the whole country.”

In 2024, Trump won the county over Kamala Harris by a razor-thin margin of roughly 500 votes. But the first congressional district broke narrowly for Harris, meaning the roughly 13-point win by Fitzpatrick — who has long described himself as a “fiercely independent voice” for his district — outpaced the top of the Republican ticket by double digits.

Charlie Dent, a former Republican representative from the neighboring Lehigh Valley, described Fitzpatrick as a political “unicorn,” noting: “He has been able to establish a brand that is separate and independent from the president.”

That puts Fitzpatrick on firmer footing than many of his Republican colleagues across the country, who are contending with an electorate that largely disapproves of Trump’s leadership.

The Fitzpatrick campaign, which did not respond to POLITICO’s request for an interview, has consistently emphasized the representative’s bipartisan credentials, with television advertisements making little reference to the Republican Party or to Trump. The campaign and groups supporting Fitzpatrick have also run a series of negative ads attacking Harvie and accusing him of corruption. An NRCC spokesman told POLITICO Harvie had a "stagnant campaign, a significant cash disadvantage, and a disqualifying record of tax hikes and misuse of taxpayer resources." Harvie has denied any allegations of wrongdoing.

Yard signs scattered throughout the district bear slogans including “Brian Fitzpatrick For All of Us” and “Brian Fitzpatrick One Community,” while campaign-sponsored billboards tout his slate of endorsements from organizations not often associated with the Republican Party, including public sector unions, animal rights and environmental groups and gun safety advocates.

“Brian is his own political force,” said Christian Nascimento, a one-time Republican congressional candidate who was until earlier this year the chair of the Montgomery County Republican Committee. “I know Democrats that vote for him just because he is willing to cross the aisle and cooperate and compromise.”

But Democratic leaders reject the characterization. On Saturday, Rep. Madeleine Dean, who represents Pennsylvania’s fourth congressional district, said Fitzpatrick was “no moderate,” calling her Republican colleague “complicit in the grotesque chaos, corruption and cruelty of this administration.”

Jeffries similarly sought to tie Fitzpatrick to Trump, telling rally-goers: “A vote for the current congressman is a vote for the status quo. Bob Harvie, a vote for him is a vote to make Congress a check and balance on an out-of-control president.”

Jeffries, who stands to become speaker if Democrats win the House next month, is not the only Democratic leader who has expended political capital for Harvie.

Shapiro, who is widely expected to sail to reelection next month against a relatively weak Republican opponent in state Treasurer Stacy Garrity, has also stumped alongside Harvie, as well as other congressional candidates in Pennsylvania this year. Many political operatives see Shapiro’s involvement in the races as an effort to show proof of concept for his own leadership ahead of a possible presidential campaign in 2028.

“[Shapiro] identified the candidates very early on who he thought would be strongly positioned to flip these seats,” Jeffries told reporters on Saturday. “Bob Harvie was among those right at the top of the list.”

Asked about his involvement in congressional races on Saturday, Shapiro told POLITICO: "Success on election night isn't just about reelecting me, but making sure we are winning all the way down the ballot.”

Shapiro has not said publicly whether he intends to run for the White House. In a debate against Garrity last week, Shapiro sidestepped a question about whether he would commit to serve a full four-year term in Harrisburg if reelected, saying: “The only thing I am focused on is running for re-election as governor.”

A Quinnipiac University poll out last week showed Shapiro with a 25-point lead over Garrity. But asked on Saturday if Democrats risked being overconfident of their chances heading into election day, the governor responded: “I run every race like I am 25 points behind, and so I’m running taking nothing for granted.”

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/11/brian-fitzpatrick-bob-harvie-pennsylvania-01115981

item.title: Newsom typically relishes battling Trump — except on undocumented students
item.description:
Gavin Newsom has rarely shied away from a fight with Donald Trump, especially over immigration.

He didn’t hesitate last year to sign into law a ban on federal immigration agents wearing masks in the state. And when he put his name on a package of legislation this year further clamping down on immigration enforcement, he said he was doing so to “push back on Trump’s Orwellian immigrant tactics.”

But when it came to a bill that would have required the state’s public universities and community colleges to make undocumented immigrant students eligible for campus employment, Newsom balked.

Trump officials, he wrote in a message explaining his vetolast month, are “quick to wreak destruction for political spectacle.” The risk of them seeking retribution against the schools was too great.

Newsom’s decision to avoid confrontation prolongs a yearslong student-led push to persuade skeptical university officials to enact a first-in-the-nation policy that would benefit the roughly 60,000 undocumented students enrolled in the three school systems. And it has deflated immigrant rights activists in his home state ahead of Newsom's likely presidential run.

“There’s disappointment that on this issue, the governor hasn't been willing to take a risk for a very important part of the California population,” said Maria Blanco, the former executive director of the UC Immigrant Legal Services Center. “Even in a progressive state like California, immigration sometimes still continues to be this third rail, especially if you're running for president.”

The governor’s unwillingness to force the issue with Trump stemmed, at least in part, from what he said in his veto message was a concern that the hiring requirement wouldn’t hold up under legal scrutiny since federal law prohibits employers from hiring undocumented workers.

Asked for comment, a spokesperson for Newsom referred to the governor’s veto message.

Advocates for the idea that students living in the country illegally should be permitted to work campus jobs have relied heavily on a legal theory a group ofUCLA law professors published in 2022 that argued the federal ban doesn’t apply to state agencies.

The theory was enough to spur discussion among the UC Board of Regents, which considered implementing a policy allowing the hires, but ultimately punted on the idea in 2024.

Rich Leib, the chair of the regents at the time who had signaled support for hiring undocumented students, said that enthusiasm on the board waned after three "established" law firms said they would not defend the university if its policy was challenged in court. With a second Trump term looming, Leib said a majority of the regents, including him, decided the timing was not right to challenge an administration that could be hostile to immigrants and voted to table the issue. They were particularly concerned, he said, about the possibility that immigration officials might be able to gain access to personal data about undocumented students on the university payroll.

“It was the most emotional experience I had as a regent because it brought you to people who were directly negatively affected by it,” Leib said, referring to students who protested at the board meeting following the vote to shelve the plan. “These are people who have done really well their whole lives. They worked really hard to get where they did, and now you're telling them they can't get a job.”

Joel Raznick, a regent emeritus who also voted for the delay, said that the possibility of Trump returning to the White House was “certainly on my mind.” Raznick, who emphasized he was not speaking on behalf of the UC, said he had been concerned about the possibility the Trump administration would respond to the hiring policy by cutting federal funding to the university – a tactic it has used in other fights with the UC – and that undocumented students could be “readily identified and deported.”

“I thought that we were doing a better service for undocumented students at that moment by preserving the university's ability to operate,” Raznick said. “Because those risks are real, as we now know.”

Anna Markowitz, president of the UCLA Faculty Association, which advocated for the hiring policy, pushed back on that rationale.

“Who are we allowing to suffer by claiming that we’re saving the institution?” she asked.

Omar Rodriguez, a spokesperson for the UC, said that the university’s “evaluation of this important issue is ongoing.” He pointed out that the UC remained neutral on the bill Newsom vetoed.

“UC has been a leader in supporting undocumented students, who are vital members of the UC community and make significant contributions to our economy and society as scholars, researchers, and future leaders,” Rodriguez said.

Along with the UC, the legislation would have applied to the California State University and community college systems. In statements, spokespeople for both systems said they also did not come out for or against the bill and support undocumented students while complying with state and federal laws.

Immigration advocates criticize Newsom and the regents for what they see as their overly cautious approach. Having a law on the books, they argue, would provide a layer of protection for the school systems if they were to have a policy allowing undocumented students to work on campus. They also point to a ruling in a state appeals court last year that found the UC’s adherence to federal law forbidding employment was discriminatory. The ruling stated that the university could not rely on fear of federal retaliation as a reason for not adopting a more permissive stance, and ordered it to “reconsider its policy based on proper criteria.”

“They're really caught in between a rock and a hard place,” said Ahilan Arulanantham, a UCLA law professor who helped write the 2022 legal theory. “They have to comply with the state court decision, and they're not going to get the benefit of any California legislation protecting them from above.”

The ruling, though, did not require the university to change its policy and did not include a deadline for the UC to comply.

“Large institutions tend to be risk adverse,” Blanco said. “And I don't think this is a climate where the UC would affirmatively go do this and then wait to be sued.”

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/11/newsom-veto-student-jobs-trump-01113178

item.title: ICE agent strikes man with car during pursuit in Texas, authorities say
item.description:
A man was hospitalized after he was struck by a vehicle driven by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent who was allegedly pursuing him and another man on Saturday, Texas law enforcement officials and ICE said.

Maj. Anthony McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's Office's Special Investigation Bureau told reporters that around 7:20 a.m. local time, law enforcement officers were called to Clay Road near Highway 6 just outside Houston after the unidentified ICE agent called 911 for an ambulance for the man, later identified by ICE as Miguel Parra-Hernandez, who was struck.

An ICE spokesperson said in a statement that the agency was attempting to arrest another man, Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national who they allege had a criminal record and a final order of removal by a judge. 

New surveillance footage shows ICE confrontation in NYC street before shooting

The ICE agent allegedly observed Mendoza-Cervantes and Parra-Hernandez, who the agency alleged was undocumented, enter a car and attempted a car stop, according to ICE.

McConnell said the ICE agent allegedly was pursuing the man and another person in their car and during the chase, the driver and the passenger left their vehicle on foot.

Surveillance video of the incident reviewed by ABC News appears to show the agent maneuvering his vehicle in the direction of the man running and striking him with the vehicle.

ICE alleged in a statement that "Parra-Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck."

Parra-Hernandez appeared to suffer a broken leg, McConnell said. He was taken to the hospital and is in ICE custody, according to ICE.

ICE didn't immediately list any criminal history about Parra-Hernandez.

McConnell referred further inquiries about the incident to ICE.

"We're here to investigate the crash," he told reporters.

Deputies were collecting video evidence from nearby buildings as part of their investigation, McConnell said. No arrests have been made.

Mendoza-Cervantes was not found as of Sunday afternoon, ICE said.

Man fatally shot by federal officer in Houston was not ICE target, DHS says

Family members of Parra-Hernandez, community leaders and officials of the immigration FIEL Houston held a news conference in Houston on Sunday.

"We have been in contact with Miguel’s family, and they are very worried about his health. He is alive but is supposed to undergo surgery for his leg, which is broken in three places," said Cesar Espinosa, executive director at FIEL Houston.

Espinosa demanded accountability from ICE and called for a transparent investigation of the incident.

"We have more questions than answers. The biggest question we have is why does this keep happening? We demand answers and transparency from all agencies involved," Espinosa said.

Harris County Precinct 4 Commissioner Lesley Briones called on ICE to provide all evidence to the Harris County Sheriff's office and to cooperate with the investigation, adding that she was "horrified" about the incident.

"We demand full transparency, accountability, and respect for the rule of law," she said in her statement.

Harris County Attorney Abbie Kamin said, "Time is of the essence in getting the facts, and the public deserves clear, accurate answers."

"ICE must cooperate fully with the local investigation," Kamin said. "My office supports Sheriff Ed Gonzalez and District Attorney Sean Teare in their ongoing independent investigation, and the Harris County Attorney's Office stands ready to assist and support these critical efforts. We will continue to monitor developments closely as the facts become clear."

The Texas incident comes two days after ICE agents shot a man inside his car with his 5-year-old son in the backseat in New York City during an attempted arrest.

Oscar Belgal, 28, is currently being held in custody and awaiting court appearances following the incident.

ICE alleged Belgal, a Dominican national, "weaponized his vehicle," and rammed ICE vehicles. Surveillance footage released by the police showed the initial encounter where two armed men approached Belgal's car and hit the driver side window.

Several New York City officials, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani, condemned ICE's actions and called on the federal government to remove them from the city.

This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/ice-agent-strikes-man-car-pursuit-texas-authorities/story?id=137162948

item.title: Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries says Democrats are on the verge of retaking the House
item.description:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries expressed growing confidence that his party will regain control of the House in November, as he visited two battleground districts in recent days to help Democratic candidates unseat Republican incumbents.

Jeffries campaigned Friday in New Jersey's competitive 7th Congressional District alongside Democratic challenger Rebecca Bennett, a Navy veteran seeking to unseat Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr. The following day, he traveled to Pennsylvania's 1st Congressional District to rally with Democrat Bob Harvie, a Bucks County commissioner challenging Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick.

The two districts are heavily suburban, fairly affluent and politically divided — and they've caused heartburn for Democrats in recent years. The moderate Fitzpatrick has a long history of outrunning other Republicans and winning crossover support since he was first elected in 2016. Control of Kean's seat has flipped twice since 2018, but he narrowly won a competitive reelection two years ago.

Democrats have invested in both races this year and view both of them as highly competitive, as they hope to take advantage of an unfavorable political environment for President Trump's party.

"We're running through the finish line. We take nothing for granted, but we're on the verge of taking back control of the House of Representatives," Jeffries told reporters following Saturday's event in Pennsylvania.

In a briefing with a small group of political reporters Wednesday, Jeffries pointed to a handful of districts in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and New York as opportunities for Democrats. He also said he plans to visit two South Texas districts.

Republicans control the House by a single-digit margin, so the outcome of the midterms could be decided by a fairly small number of races. Jeffries declined to predict how many seats his party could gain in November.

"I'm very confident that we're going to take back the majority, but it remains to be seen what that looks like in terms of the number of seats that we pick up, which is going to depend on the conditions that exist over the next few weeks," he said in the briefing.

During the rally in Bucks County, a perennial swing county that supported Mr. Trump by a razor-thin margin in 2024 after years of narrow Democratic victories, Harvie said: "It is not an accident that Hakeem Jeffries is here tonight."

"He knows what we're going to do with this district. He knows the potential," he said.

Fitzpatrick's campaign told CBS News that the Republican lawmaker "is aware of Hakeem's visit, he still considers him a friend, and he looks forward to working with him in a bipartisan manner in the 120th Congress."

"Leader Jeffries is doing what he needs to do, and Brian completely understands that," the campaign's statement continued.

Fitzpatrick, who is seeking a sixth term, has cultivated a moderate image and put distance between himself and Mr. Trump, voting with House Democrats to rescind tariffs on Canada and restrict the Iran war. He also voted against final passage of the Trump administration's signature "Big, Beautiful Bill" last year. Most recently, he pushed back last week on the president's plan to buy diesel from Russia.

Democrats have argued Fitzpatrick hasn't consistently opposed the president's agenda, pointing to an earlier vote in favor of the "Big, Beautiful Bill." Fitzpatrick has said he voted against the final legislation after the Senate added steeper Medicaid cuts.

Judi Reiss, a Democratic local elected official in Lower Makefield Township, Pennsylvania, told CBS News at Saturday's rally with Jeffries and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro that she has "no personal animosity toward [Fitzpatrick] whatsoever, but he hasn't done anything. He's been a rubber stamp for Donald Trump."

"He has not been independent, and it's very disappointing," said Reiss, who sought the 2020 Democratic nomination for Fitzpatrick's seat but dropped out before the primary.

Still, Fitzpatrick has survived on challenging terrain in the past — and overperformed other Republicans. Vice President Kamala Harris narrowly won his district in 2024, but Fitzpatrick won reelection the same year by a more than 12-point margin.

The Cook Political Report rated the Pennsylvania district "Leans Republican" on Friday, down from its previous "Likely Republican" assessment.

Bucks County resident Bill Craig, a Republican who plans to vote for Fitzpatrick, told CBS News he believes Harvie has a "slim chance" of winning the district, but he expects the race to be close due to heavy Democratic turnout.

"Brian Fitzpatrick could cure cancer right now, and they still wouldn't vote for them," Craig said. "He's very middle-of-the-road. They're trying to paint him as some kind of MAGA psycho."

Jeffries visited Fitzpatrick's district a day after campaigning for Bennett across the Delaware River, in a New Jersey seat that the Cook Political report sees as Democratic-leaning — a shift after it called the race a toss-up as recently as last month.

The GOP incumbent there, Kean, is seeking a third term representing a district that stretches from the New York City suburbs to the Pennsylvania border, with Mr. Trump's Bedminster golf club sitting in the middle. He was first elected after the district was made slightly redder in 2022, and defeated Democratic Rep. Tom Malinowski.

House Speaker Mike Johnson also campaigned with Kean in recent weeks.

Jeffries' campaign stops illustrate the importance of suburban congressional districts that could help determine which party controls the House next year.

In last week's briefing with reporters, the Democratic leader described all four competitive Republican-held districts in Pennsylvania as Democratic pickup opportunities. In addition to Fitzpatrick's seat, Democrats are targeting a northeastern Pennsylvania district and two seats in eastern and central Pennsylvania.

He also singled out the race in New York's 17th Congressional District, where Democrat Cait Conley is challenging Republican Rep. Mike Lawler.

Jeffries to campaign in South Texas races

Meanwhile, Democrats are defending two competitive districts in South Texas, and have signaled they plan to go on offense in two GOP-held districts in the region. 

Republicans made substantial gains among Latinos in 2024, especially in South Texas, where some counties that were once Democratic strongholds became light-red.

Jeffries argued that Latino voters could swing back to Democrats, pointing to concerns over the cost of living and the Trump administration's aggressive immigration policies.

He said the political environment has changed dramatically in the Rio Grande Valley, where Democratic Reps. Henry Cuellar and Vicente Gonzalez are seeking reelection. 

Jeffries said he also plans to campaign in the coming weeks for two Texas Democrats who hope to unseat Republicans. Tejano music star Bobby Pulido is running against Republican Rep. Monica De La Cruz in a toss-up district, and Democrat Johnny Garcia is challenging Republican nominee Carlos De La Cruz in a seat that's viewed as redder.

The Democratic leader also rejected the notion that newly drawn Republican congressional maps in Texas and Florida would deliver the substantial gains GOP strategists had initially anticipated.

"Under no circumstances are Republicans winning five seats in Texas or four seats in Florida," Jeffries told CBS News last week.

The National Republican Congressional Committee has disputed Democrats' increasingly optimistic assessments of the battleground map, pointing to Republican campaign resources and ground game efforts in competitive districts.

If Democrats regain control of the House, Jeffries would be positioned to become the first Black speaker of the House in American history.

While the party that doesn't control the White House almost always performs well in the midterms, the exact result is tougher to predict. In the 2022 midterms, when Republicans were buoyed by former President Joe Biden's unpopularity, predictions of a sweeping GOP wave failed to materialize. Republicans narrowly won control of the House but failed to recapture the Senate until two years later.

Asked by CBS News whether Democrats risk that kind of election night disappointment, Jeffries acknowledged the outcome will depend on the political climate and spending.

He said that while the current environment appears favorable to Democrats, the amount of money being spent by Republican-aligned political groups could ultimately limit the number of seats his party gains.

House Republicans' campaign committee had more cash on hand than the group's Democratic counterpart at the end of August. 

Jeffries disputed suggestions that Republicans hold an overwhelming financial advantage in House battlegrounds, arguing that Democrats are effectively at parity when spending by candidates, committees and outside groups is considered together.

On the GOP side, Johnson is also barnstorming frontline districts as Republicans fight to maintain their majority — and look for opportunities to unseat vulnerable Democrats. 

Johnson said the other day he expects to visit about 40 districts this month.

In recent days, Johnson has visited Michigan and Pennsylvania with incumbent Republicans, and campaigned alongside two Iowa Republicans who are aiming to retain GOP-held districts: Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Joe Mitchell.

He also campaigned last week in Ohio with Derek Merrin, who is hoping to unseat longtime Democratic Rep. Marcy Kaptur in a toss-up district. It's a rematch of 2024, when Merrin lost to Kaptur by around 2,400 votes.

During his visit to Ohio, Johnson said he expects control of the House to be determined by at least 22 seats that he sees as "jump-balls." He has expressed optimism that Republicans can retain their majority.

"This will come down to the outcome of about 22 districts around the country, and I believe we can win those," Johnson told reporters late last month.

Mr. Trump has also continued an aggressive campaign schedule aimed at boosting Republican candidates. Jeffries said he welcomes his increased involvement.

"The more Donald Trump campaigns for Republicans across the country, the better for the opportunity for Democrats to further convince the American people that we actually are the only ones determined to make life more affordable for them," Jeffries said.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jeffries-democrats-control-house-battleground-races/

item.title: 利雅得机场周日再遭袭 胡塞连续两天攻击沙特首都空港
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

沙特阿拉伯首都利雅得的哈立德国王国际机场星期日（10月11日）再次遭到袭击，这是该机场连续第二天遇袭。沙特领导的也门联军表示，一枚“不明抛射物”击中机场4号航站楼，引发火灾并造成人员受伤，但暂未公布具体伤者人数。

也门胡塞武装随后宣称对袭击负责。就在当天稍早，胡塞已公开警告航空公司、机场工作人员和旅客不要使用沙特机场及领空，称这些设施已经成为其军事行动区域，但表示麦加和麦地那机场不在警告范围内。

星期日的袭击发生在利雅得机场遭受重大伤亡攻击仅一天之后。星期六，一枚导弹击中机场客运航站楼，造成超过300人受伤。最初公布的死亡人数为12人，一名印度籍伤者星期日伤重不治后，死亡人数升至13人。胡塞武装也宣称实施了星期六的袭击。

利雅得机场目前仍受到严重航班中断影响，多家航空公司取消或调整往返沙特的航班。连续两天攻击同一座大型国际机场，也进一步加剧外界对沙特领空和民航安全的担忧。欧盟航空安全机构此前已经扩大对沙特领空的风险警告。

袭击发生之际，沙特支持的也门政府军正在加大针对胡塞武装的军事行动。胡塞则持续以导弹和无人机袭击沙特境内目标。美国总统川普星期六表示，正考虑美国是否加入沙特针对胡塞武装的军事行动，并计划与沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼通话。

与此同时，利雅得正在举行大型国际能源会议。连续发生的机场袭击不仅直接冲击沙特民航，也使也门战事进一步外溢至沙特首都，并增加红海航运和地区能源供应面临的安全风险。

item.title: 他为什么敢这样议论马车安全问题
item.description:
来源: 
后代聊斋

车辆安全出问题，有争议时怎么办？

两千多年前，古人早就有了教科书式的应对方法。

春秋末年，前493年，晋、郑爆发“铁之战”（铁即铁丘，位今河南濮阳西北部）。

战争缘起晋国内乱。

春秋中晚期，晋国公室大权旁落，范氏、中行氏、智氏、赵氏、魏氏、韩氏六卿专政，内斗不已。晋定公十三年（前497），赵氏宗主赵鞅（即赵简子）诛杀了胳膊肘向外拐的同宗远亲赵午。赵午又是中行氏的外甥，中行氏便以赵鞅肆意诛杀大夫为名，联合范氏攻打赵氏，赵鞅打不过，逃进根据地晋阳，被围困。晋定公听信范氏、中行氏的话，认为赵鞅叛晋，也出兵攻打赵鞅。

另外三家智氏、魏氏、韩氏不希望看到范氏、中行氏灭赵之后坐大，遂联合出兵攻打范氏、中行氏，同时向晋定公陈情，说赵鞅杀赵午只是赵氏宗族内部清除异己，并不是反晋。于是，晋定公反戈攻打范氏、中行氏，范氏、中行氏打不过，逃进范氏的封邑朝歌，赵鞅则乘胜反攻。

朝歌被围，城中粮食告急。这时候，为了争霸，唯恐晋国不乱的齐国，联合郑国支援范氏、中行氏——就在这一年八月，齐国调拨了一千车粮食，由郑国两位大夫率军护送到朝歌给范氏和中行氏。

赵鞅得知，决定拦截，于是，赵、郑两军在铁丘展开了遭遇战。

严格来讲，赵鞅手上只有赵氏私兵，而郑国大夫率领的是郑国军队，兵力上碾压赵军。赵鞅只能不断给将士们打气，并许诺杀敌立功者可得封地、封官等奖赏，奴隶也可得自由身。

战斗开始，赵鞅身先士卒，被郑军刺中肩膀，倒在战车里。危急之时，给赵鞅充当“车右”的卫国太子蒯聩奋起神勇，斩杀郑军，救了赵鞅。（车右：战车上站在主将右边，负责警戒和保卫的将士；蒯聩当时因为本国内乱而逃亡到晋国，投奔赵鞅。）

就这样，赵军上下齐心，浴血奋战，竟以少胜多，打得郑军狼狈逃窜，还缴获了齐国的一千车粮食。

战后，也许是被自己感动了，赵鞅感慨地说：“我肩膀受伤，趴在箭囊上吐血，但还是保持鼓声不断，士气受到鼓舞，这才打赢了这场战斗，论功劳，我是第一。”

蒯聩也自豪地说：“我在车上救了您，又跳下车去追击敌人，我是所有车右中功劳最大的。”

这时，给赵鞅驾车的邮良说：“我两靷将绝，吾能止之，我，御之上也。”（《左传·哀公二年》）我勒马的两根带子快断了，我还能死死控制住车，我是所有司机中功劳最大的。

此言一出，几乎所有人都表示怀疑：“不是吧，这种情况怎么可能出现？你是范氏、中行氏派来造谣惑众的吧？”

怀疑归怀疑，但包括赵鞅在内，上上下下并没有人把邮良的嘴堵住。邮良也不争辩，只是默默干了一件事：

驾而乘材，两靷皆绝。（《左传·哀公二年》）

众目睽睽之下，邮良重新驾上马车，车上只载了点木材，马一动，两条带子就全都断了。事实证明，刚才那两根带子确实快断了，邮良凭着自己高超的驾车技术，才没让马、车分崩离析。

可见，两千五百年前，古人早就懂得，当有人说车辆有问题时，只要在同等条件下重做一次实验，就能将真相公诸于众。

而马车出现安全问题这种事，后世有了一个专用名词：

衔橛之变。

出自汉赋名家司马相如的《上书谏猎》（后被收入《古文观止》）。

当时司马相如二进宫为郎官，汉武帝曾召他陪着到长杨宫打猎。那段时间汉武帝痴迷于猎杀熊和野猪，为了展示自己的雄风，常纵马抛下卫士去追逐野兽，司马相如觉得这样太冒险，遂上疏加以劝谏。

劝谏分三层意思，首先，司马相如认为，人有大力士，兽类中也有特别凶猛的，万一当面遇到，掉头不及，身边又没有卫士，后果不堪设想。

第二段，他就提到“衔橛之变”。

且夫清道而后行，中路而驰，犹时有衔橛之变。况乎涉丰草，骋丘墟，前有利兽之乐，而内无存变之意，其为害也不亦难矣。

衔，即“马勒”，横在马嘴里的嚼子，制动、控速用的；橛，即“车钩心”，车轴相连的钩心木。“衔”如果断了，马就失控；“橛”如果断了，车就会解体。司马相如把这种情况称为“衔橛之变”。

平时皇帝出行，都会提前封路、清道，走的都是平坦大路，饶是这样，偶尔都会发生“衔橛之变”。狩猎时要跨越茂密草丛，奔驰在崎岖不平的路况上，甚至是无路的丘墟之间，眼里只盯着前面野兽的动静，心中根本没有应急准备，翻车是随时可能发生的事，太危险了。

最后，司马相如说，俗话说“家累千金，坐不垂堂”，普通的富人家，都知道不要在屋檐下坐着，以免被掉落的瓦片砸到头，陛下以“万乘之重”，如此不看重安全问题，此举实不可取。

就差一句“陛下就算不为自己着想，也要为社稷百姓着想，大汉不能没有你啊”了。

还真是皇帝不急，太监也不急，御用文人倒急了。

司马相如毕竟是郎官，食君之禄，尽忠职守，也是应该的。只是，他可以大胆说出“衔橛之变”，也不会被扣上一顶“抹黑大汉”的帽子，这充分说明，在汉民族历史上，某些所谓的“封建王朝”，马车的安全问题，也是可以用人话公开讨论的。

2026年10月11日

item.title: 一架钢琴的陕北往事
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

“文化大革命”期间，大批城市知识青年被安排到农村插队落户。一位名叫高曼的北京女知青，却带着一件不同寻常的行李来到陕北：一架德国制造的立式钢琴。

从县城到插队的村庄，需要翻越周家屹崂的大塬。由于没有公路，钢琴只能依靠人力搬运。八个老乡抬着沉重的木箱，遇到陡坡还得增加人手，前拉后推，走走停停，才将它运进村里。

箱子打开后，村民们十分惊奇，而当地干部却对此提出了批评。当时，知识青年下乡被要求接受贫下中农再教育，钢琴容易被视为资产阶级生活方式的象征。一个城市青年竟然把钢琴带到贫困山区，被认为是没有做好参加农业劳动的思想准备。

然而，村民们并不这样看。他们发现，高曼能够用钢琴弹奏出美妙的音乐，便安排她到村里的小学教书，教孩子们唱歌。

由于钢琴也被用于革命样板戏伴奏，高曼又会弹奏《红灯记》《东方红》《南泥湾》等革命歌曲，围绕钢琴的政治争议逐渐平息。

高曼就这样在陕北的一个小山村安顿下来。

她住在小学旁边的两间窑洞里，一间作为卧室和备课室，另一间放置钢琴。除了给孩子们上音乐课，她还经常弹奏贺绿汀的《牧童短笛》以及贝多芬的《致爱丽丝》《月光奏鸣曲》等作品。

在当时的政治环境下，这些西方古典音乐作品可能被批判为“封资修”音乐。不过，在这个偏僻的山村，村民们并不在意作品的政治属性。

他们渐渐习惯了每天听见钢琴声。有时高曼晚上没有弹琴，第二天便有人询问她是不是病了。附近的人提起这个村庄，一时想不起村名，就称它为“有钢琴的那个村”。

高曼自幼学习钢琴。1949年，她家的邻居离开大陆时，将这架德国钢琴低价卖给了她的父母。父母都在大学任教，发现女儿有音乐天赋，便在她三岁时为她请来钢琴教师。

由于自幼体弱，高曼很少与其他孩子在外面玩耍，钢琴逐渐成为她生活中不可缺少的一部分。“文化大革命”期间，她虽然身体有病，仍然未能免于下乡插队。临行前，她坚持要把钢琴带走，父母只好请人制作木箱，将钢琴运往陕北。

来到农村后，高曼不仅教孩子们唱歌，也经常接待前来听琴的村民。

有一次，她弹奏《北风吹》，一个名叫四丫的女孩听着听着，突然流下眼泪，随后放声大哭，跑出了窑洞。

高曼后来才知道，四丫刚满十三岁，父母已经为她订下婚事，不久就要出嫁。

四丫没有看过《白毛女》，却在《北风吹》的旋律中听出了自己的悲伤。她无法自主决定婚姻，即将在尚未成年的时候离开家庭，与一个陌生男子共同生活。

这件事使高曼对农村女孩的处境有了更直接的认识。她曾因下乡插队中断自己的音乐道路而感到痛苦，但与四丫相比，她至少接受过教育，还拥有自己喜爱的钢琴。

后来，四丫还是按照父母的安排出嫁了。高曼再弹《北风吹》时，便常常想起这个女孩。

高曼在村里还结识了一位下放干部老金。老金原本在司法部门工作，出身京剧世家，擅长老旦唱腔。她几乎每天都到高曼的窑洞里，用钢琴伴奏练习《红灯记》《沙家浜》等剧目的唱段。

当地村民也加入进来，请高曼为他们熟悉的道情伴奏。渐渐地，这间窑洞成了村里的音乐活动场所，革命歌曲、京剧唱段、民歌和地方曲艺，都曾在这里响起。

插队的第四年，老金调回北京。回京后，她通过多方联系，帮助高曼办理了病退手续，使她终于获得返回北京的机会。

就在高曼准备离开时，公社中学找到她，希望将钢琴留下，供学生们上音乐课使用。

高曼起初十分为难。这架钢琴已经陪伴她二十多年，从北京来到陕北，又在艰苦的农村生活中陪伴她度过了数年。如今能够返回北京，她原本希望将钢琴一同带走。

但她想到，自己教过的许多小学生已经升入公社中学。如果留下钢琴，孩子们便能够继续学习音乐。

经过考虑，高曼最终决定将钢琴无偿赠送给学校。

运琴那天，她将钢琴仔细擦拭，又取下炕上的棉毯，将容易碰撞的部位包裹起来。学校派来一辆手扶拖拉机，高曼一路扶着钢琴，防止它在颠簸的山路上受到损坏。

到达学校后，她查看了安放钢琴的窑洞，指导教师们将琴摆好，试了试音，又向接手的音乐教师交代了使用和保养的注意事项。

随后，高曼向学校告辞。

校长提出派拖拉机送她回去，她以还要到公社购买东西为由婉拒。

离开学校后，高曼独自登上对面的山坡，在那里坐了很久，望着安放钢琴的那间窑洞，流下了眼泪。

当年，她执意将钢琴从北京带到陕北。如今，她终于可以返回北京，却将陪伴自己二十多年的钢琴留在了这个山村。

高曼回京后，再也没有回到这里。

那架钢琴在公社中学继续使用了几年，后来逐渐损坏。由于当地没有能够维修钢琴的专业人员，学校只能将其闲置。时间一长，钢琴最终不知去向。

只有那些曾经在高曼伴奏下唱过歌的孩子，还记得童年时，陕北山村里曾经响起过一架德国钢琴的声音。

资料来源：陈幼民《也是一首歌》

item.title: 我的高考：1978
item.description:
来源: 
新三届

我复员回到北京时，是带着伤回来的。复员前在炊事班，有一次蒸包子，笼屉巨大，得几个人抬到大铁锅上。到了锅前，我双手抬着笼屉，背身蹬上灶台，往后挪，一脚踩进沸水翻滚的大铁锅里。当时是冬天，穿着大头皮鞋，开始还说“没事没事”，不一会，刺啦刺啦地疼，站不住了。左脚脚踝处烫出一个十厘米高、约五厘米宽的烫伤，很严重。直到回北京，还是一瘸一拐的。

这是1978年3月下旬，离高考还有四个月。

01

我回来就是为考大学。从1966年全国取消高考，大学就瘫痪了。几年后开始小规模招生，实行“群众推荐、领导批准、学校复审”的办法，实际上是政治标准第一，不管文化水平，说不上是正规的大学教育。1977年恢复了高考，举国震动。从理论上讲，这是给了全国所有青年一个平等的机会。1978年是第二次全国统考，热度直线上升。但部队特殊，仍不能自由报名，所以我要求复员回家。

只有四个月时间，怎么复习？李大兴的妈妈于川阿姨把我介绍到师大附中，跟高考班一块听课。当时大兴在那儿上高中。听了几次，收获不大。回到母校126中，老师们让我上这里的高考复习班。别看126中名不见经传，高考班的老师可都是一流的。我一下就抓住了重点。

6月初，家里来了个陌生青年小孟，自报家门是我妈妈的朋友李亦云的儿子。他说：中央戏剧学院本月底考试，有戏剧文学系，不考数学。他是69届初中毕业去了内蒙古，根本不会数学，所以想考中戏戏文系。他妈妈说我们家书多，让他来借书。我们家书虽多，跟文艺沾边的可没有。小孟悻悻而返。

我却感了兴趣。数学是我的最弱项，也怕考试。另外，听说有的人考试会怯场，比如一进考场手就抖，连笔都拿不住，最后只好弃考。我可以先参加一下中戏的考试，考验考验自己，获取一些经验。最后，文艺界对我来说完全陌生，凑个热闹也挺好玩儿的。于是我去报了名。

中戏考试分初试和复试两个阶段。我没有复习，因为完全不知道应该复习什么。到了初试那天，进去就考，没什么负担，基本都是一些语文、政治和戏剧常识，其中有一道专业题是10分，问：你读过哪些莎士比亚的剧本？请试述其中一个的剧情概要。我绞尽脑汁想了半天，想出一个剧名《皆大欢喜》，至于剧情，一无所知。现在看，这不是白给的一道题吗？但没文化，没办法，白白丢了10分。

考完就不管它了，继续复习全国高考的科目。有一天和张朴到国子监首都图书馆去复习，二人都是懒汉，闲聊天为主，张朴忽然说：“哎？今天是中戏公布初试结果的日子吧？”“哦！可不是嘛！”“还不看看去？”“肯定没戏。”

中戏在棉花胡同，很近。我俩骑车去的。初试合格的考生的名字都用准考证号码代替，写在大字报纸上，在校门对面的墙上贴了好几张，一共400多人。我们俩分别看，忽听张朴叫起来：“晓阳，这不是你嘛！”我循声望去，眼睛都模糊了，果然是我。

在这几张榜的旁边，是一位落选考生写的真正的大字报，抨击学院考试舞弊的，说通过初试的400人全是走后门。我心里暗笑：至少我就不是走后门的，让我去走我也不知道后门在哪儿？

这次考试是十几年来中戏戏文系第一次招生，全国设6个考试点，共4000多人参加。考题那么简单，还刷掉了十分之九，可见当时考生水平之低。

初试侥幸通过，我上心了，可离复试只有两天，怎么准备？实在摸不到头脑。

文学所的劳洪叔叔说：不知道莎士比亚，怎么能上戏剧学院呢？现补也来不及了，我给你讲几个莎剧的故事吧。我说：复试肯定不会再考这种题了。劳洪叔叔不是研究戏剧的，不清楚这里的门道，束手无策。

我妈妈的朋友徐滨阿姨知道了，说太巧了，我们楼里住着一位剧协的领导，前年地震时两家地震棚挨着，熟悉了，可以问问他。

于是徐滨阿姨带我去了肖家。肖叔叔是延安鲁艺出身，高高胖胖的，很和蔼。他夫人曹阿姨也在文艺口工作，以前是太岳军区文工团的，说我父亲看过他们演出，对我很亲热。肖叔叔说：戏剧学院的考试情况我不了解呀……你呀，就好好读毛的《讲话》。我向他借参考书，他走进书房好一会才出来，借我一本苏联的《加里宁论文艺》。

回到徐滨阿姨家，她女儿和平说：加里宁论文艺？这有什么用！和平是她们家族子女中的学霸，什么都懂。听了她的话，那本书我就放在她家没拿。

后来复试时，文艺理论一门，共5道大题（论述题），每题20分，其中3道题出自《讲话》，我都不会答。如果当初老老实实听肖叔叔的话，把《讲话》看几遍，那就是小菜一碟。我这才明白：他虽不了解中戏的考试，却非常了解当时整个文艺界的大形势，只要沾文艺，都得围着《讲话》转。

几年后我参加工作，因为在文联系统，知道了不少事，也才听说：剧协与中戏一向有矛盾，中戏在行政上也不归剧协领导，所以剧协的人不知道中戏考试的情况，是顺理成章的事。那天肖叔叔对我说的，都是实在话，并不是敷衍。至于《加里宁论文艺》，在那余悸犹存的环境里，是安全性最高的，他不敢把“封资修”的书籍借给一个青年，而且看了封资修也帮不上这种奇葩考试。

我就这样绝望地参加了复试。

考写作那天，是在鼓楼上的楼洞子里，两头通透，穿堂风呼呼而过。作文题目《旅途上》。我正凝神构思，左后方传来吭吭唧唧的声音，扭头一看，是一个戴眼镜的小男孩发出的，他在试卷上写了标题，用的碳素墨水，标题下画了很多黑道子，手攥钢笔，蹙眉思考，嘴里不自觉发出声音。我几次怒视他，想引起他注意，别再发声，可毫无作用。但由此记住了这张面孔。

后来我上了人民大学，基础外语学日语。我们这个日语班由几个系的同学合成，第一节课结束，我站起来一看，就看见了这张面孔：戴眼镜、清秀、头发又密又干又硬。我走过去说：“你考过戏剧学院吧？”“是啊是啊！”他叫十庆，我把鼓楼楼洞子里的事讲说一遍，十庆大笑。我们俩“一见钟情”，立刻就玩儿到一块了。

口试是在中戏的教学楼，一个一个叫进去问。等候的考生，全部集中在楼门内的门洞里，门洞两边摞着体操垫，人们有坐有站。我是年龄最小的，穿一件当兵的绿衬衣、的确良裤子、“片儿懒”，土气稚嫩。其他人，大部分都装扮入时、顾影自怜、顾盼自雄，一看就跟文艺界沾边儿。

虽互不相识，但交谈热烈，内容则为我闻所未闻，什么赵丹如何、金山如何、谢芳怎么了、白杨怎么了……说起来就像他们家三叔或二姨。有一位梳着大分头的男子，得有30岁了，叼着烟斗，说他是某某剧团的编剧，人问写过什么？他自豪地回答：“《鸡鸣山下》。”声音低沉浑厚，在门洞中嗡嗡作响。

最能侃的姓米，不到三十岁，一米九几的细高杆儿，坐在体操垫上。他说：“写作考试里出了一篇奇文，是咱们这里岁数最小的人写的，写北京一女的，嫁给香港人，飞机一落地，直接就给送妓院去了……旅途上！”实在惊人！几乎不可想象。当时，那个地方在所有大陆人的脑袋里，还是遥远而神秘的另一个世界、资本主义的地狱或天堂，谁又能想象那里发生的事情、并把它写进堂堂艺术院校考试的作文里呢？

后来十庆告诉我，那篇作文就是他写的，不及格。

短短的等候口试期间，我们听众只是听，就已将素昧平生的米先生的个人履历，了解得一清二楚：家是科学院的，住中关村科学院宿舍，听来像是干部子弟。他说，杜润生在中科院干校时放猪，每天手捧红宝书，孜孜不倦地学习。群众起了疑惑，夺过红宝书一看，红塑料书皮里包的是《金瓶梅》。米先生自小热爱体育，是北京田径队的专业跳高运动员，后来腿摔断了，复员在工厂里当工人。他的最爱是《约翰·克里斯朵夫》，谈起此书，情不能禁，在体操垫子上手舞足蹈地讲述了其中一个片段，简直像电影一样精彩……

几个月后，我在人民大学的操场上上体育课时，忽然看到了高挑的米先生，他成了人大的一名体育老师。敢情这么有才的人也没考上中戏啊！我又走过去，对他说：“米老师，您也考过戏剧学院吧？”他可不像十庆那么随和，听闻此言，脖子一拧，再也不理我了。

口试的情况就不要说了，我胡说八道了一通。几个老师都很善良，没打我。

最终从400多考生中录取了40多名，又是一个十分之一。我、十庆、宋毅都落榜了，我们仨考上了人民大学。米老师成了人大体育教员。

于川阿姨说：“考戏剧学院干嘛？那不是正经学校。人民大学多好！”

02

进入7月，天气炎热。我拿起复习材料就浑身无力、眼皮打架，真他妈无聊！骑上自行车奔王府井，在书店里一泡一两个钟头。市场上的商品多起来了，社会经过长期动荡，似乎在慢慢疗伤、慢慢恢复元气。王府井南口那个存在了二十年的报刊亭，仍只有孤零零几种骗人的报刊，贫乏单调，我唯一买过的，是《人民画报》。

它的北边、东单二条口上，巨型公共厕所人流不断，连解大手都不容易找到坑儿，暑热一蒸，臊气冲天。但是市民的穿着有了变化，花裙子不时闪现，烫头的女性也有了，60年代华君武的一幅讽刺漫画曾把这叫“卷毛狮子狗”。

即使是面临决定命运的高考，我也必须去游泳。本身爱好就少，社会上又几乎没有“娱乐”这个词，再不扎个猛子扑腾扑腾，非疯喽！到手一张内部电影票？跨越千山万水也要去。路过电影院，头都不抬一下，因为如果看到新片广告，肯定是大烂片，恨不得把导演给毙了。与张朴去国子监首都图书馆，名义上是复习，其实质更类似春游，坐在草地上，中心议题是侃大山，他知道的事多，我听不够。

有亲友来家慰问我，千叮咛万嘱咐：要劳逸结合，不能太用功了，某某家的某某某，因为长时间伏案，得了胸什么炎，某某家的某某某，患上严重失眠症……我从他们的谈论中，才意识到高考在中国人的心目中分量有多重，几乎是决定生死的人生一战。再看我，稀里咣当，晃来晃去，该吃吃该喝喝，到点儿就睡，该起不起，对那些得胸什么炎的人徒生崇敬，可就是着急不起来。

我妈妈心里急，表面上一句话不说，等我考上大学，她才开言：哎呀，那时候看你呀，一会儿游泳去啦，一会儿又干什么去啦，晚上挺晚才回来……我心想这哪儿像要考大学呀？

我中学的班主任杨老太太，是语文教师，她不教高考复习班，但关心我，有一次我们写押题作文，她专门把我写的拿来看了。后来在校园里碰到我，说：“你怎么当兵当傻了？写的那作文，那叫什么呀！越写越退步。”我说：“没有文化的军队是愚蠢的军队，而我就是愚蠢军队里的一个。”其实我心里忽悠一下子，对杨老师的话十分重视。

我们复员大兵的档案在东城区复转军人办公室，每星期组织一次学习，这中间不断分配工作。国家是劫后重生，各方面都需要人，所以这批人分配的都是机关和事业单位，这在以前是很少见的（一般都是工厂）。我已说明要考大学，暂不参加分配。有一天负责人问我，现在《中国青年报》有两个名额，你去不去？我说不去。他很惊讶，说：“这还不去？大学毕了业不也就是去这种单位吗？……告诉你啊，这是最后一批事业单位，以后就全是工厂了。”意思说，考不上大学就得当工人了。

他的话有道理。但我心里权衡了一下，还是想上学。既然好不容易来了机会，就必须抓住它，不然将来会后悔。如果考不上，那是自己的问题，也就认命了。

高考在7月20日开始，连考三天。

我的考场在北小街的一所中学（164中）。进了考场，我一点儿也不慌。我从小一直都是这样，其实我功课学得并不扎实，而且偏科，但逢到考试，却比平时聪明，平时不会做的题，考试时会，不考试了，又不会了。

上一年的高考，语文是写作文《我在这战斗的一年里》。所以一年来，大家都拼命练习命题作文。今年语文试卷打开一看，没有作文，百分之四十是语文基础知识，百分之六十叫“缩写文章”，就是给你一篇文章，让你缩写成多少字。好多人一下就懵了，因为不在复习范围内，不知该怎么办。对我来说这却简单了，找重点呗。写作文带有创造性，有时写得好，有时写不好，不稳定。缩写你只要把重点都找到，保证满分。找重点还不容易？

结果大家都说今年的语文最难，考分普遍偏低。

我语文考了93分，数学28分。真实反映了我的学习状况。

过分数线的考生要体检。在医院里排着大长队，都是年轻人，个个喜气洋洋。排我前面的两个小伙子互相认识，一直在聊天。“你语文多少分？”“61。”“不错啊！我才46。”“咱们这里有一个人考了93分，北京市最高分。”“不可能！我听说的最高的是78分。今年语文太难了……”

高考结束，有一天我到苏州胡同找中学同学储兵玩儿，他已在春季上了邮电学院。他正摆弄相机，让我站在他家单元门口，给我照了张相。洗出来一看，我比四个月前瘦了许多，很疲惫的样子。我才知道：虽说这四个月没下苦功，但心理压力还是很大的，精神处于紧张状态，像病了一场，不知不觉衣带渐宽。

在人民大学同届生中，我算岁数小的。同学中有煤矿工、装卸工、修钢笔的、澡堂子的、裁缝、农民、公社书记、地委组织部副部长、工厂副厂长、还有刚从监狱出来的。年龄最小的16岁，最大的超过30。我们班的学生支书28岁，已有四个孩子。

这样复杂的学生成分，在全世界的大学里也是独一无二的。这是一个国家长期处于不正常状态后，出现的奇观。

所有人的命运，都被这次高考改变了。

2025年3月28日

item.title: 美议员：美俄柴油协议违法
item.description: 周日，民主党和共和党议员质疑华盛顿和莫斯科就俄罗斯柴油供应达成的协议的合法性，声称该协议违反了美国国会通过的一项法律。
